ateret-zekenim/1:_: On the 14th of first Adar — not the 15th, even though in second Adar they practice feast and joy on both (Beit Yosef and Hagahot Maimoniot in the name of Semak); however regarding prohibition of melacha there is no prohibition on the first since on the second too there is no prohibition except where they practiced (Beit Yosef in the name of Semak). And some say they practice not to do melacha on Purim Katan both days (Abudraham) and we do not practice so. May the Almighty send a redeemer to Judah and Israel and the days of Purim not be annulled even after the Temple is rebuilt, amen amen.
eliyah-rabbah/1:_: (a) even in the form and so on. But Ignostics are used to everything, and they are allowed to be filled and do not say about miracles:
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] One does not say Tachanun on the 14th and 15th of Adar I, and the law of fasting and eulogizing on those days. Containing one paragraph. On the 14th and 15th of Adar I we do not fall on our faces and we do not say the psalm "Ya'ancha Heaven beyom tzarah," and on those days it is forbidden to eulogize and to fast; but other matters are not practiced on them. And some say that even eulogy and fasting are permitted. {Rama: The custom follows the first view. Some say one is obligated to increase in feasting and joy on the 14th of Adar I (Tur in the name of the Rif}; however we do not practice thus. Nevertheless one should increase somewhat at the meal to satisfy those who are stringent (Hagahot Maimuni in the name of SeMaK}. "But the good-hearted has a continual feast" (Proverbs 15:15}.}
shaarei-teshuvah/1:א: (א) 14th and 15th of Adar I — see Peri Megadim and Kaf HaChayyim.
shaarei-teshuvah/1:ב: On the 14th. Avodat HaTodah and Avodat Yisrael brought in the name of Hagahot Tashbetz that Rabbeinu Yechiel of Paris was accustomed to increase in the meal and invite people as the language of the Mishnah implies "there is no difference between Adar" etc., and he explained Rama concludes "a good-hearted person has a continual feast" — see Rashi Yevamot who wrote Maharam z"l in wisdom established a closing like an opening — two "tamid" in order — he opened at the start of his glosses "I set the Almighty before me always" and closed "a good-hearted person has a continual feast" etc. see there. It appears to me since he wanted to conclude with a good word and timely word he used excellent language of the verse for joy and "good heart" meaning it is good to make feast in both Adars; possibly this is Taz's intent in what he wrote Rama concludes well etc., his intent as written; also there is a hint that the word "feast" "good" in gematria is first Adar; also possible per what is written siman 670 in gloss 2 regarding Chanukah that some say there is some mitzvah in increasing meals etc. and they practice saying songs and praises at the meal they increase — then it is seudat mitzvah see there, and from there we learn here too when one increases somewhat in the meal to satisfy stringent ones — practice saying songs and praises then certainly seudat mitzvah; and to hint this he concludes "a good-hearted person has a continual feast" per what we say in Arakhin 11: from where is the essence of song from Torah etc. — any service that is in joy and good heart is called song see there Rashi brings from Yeshayahu 65 behold My servants shall sing from goodness of heart see there Tosafot we find also regarding Torah as Rashi wrote in Ruth that there is in midrash "and his heart was good" in Torah and so Shabbat 63 "and He will make your heart good" on Torah study but not written explicitly see there; therefore he said "good heart continual feast" meaning in goodness of heart i.e. songs and praises and Torah study continual feast; per what is written elsewhere on "and Israel encamped before the mountain" meaning the evil inclination was removed from them therefore Rashi explained "encamped as one man with one heart" per "with all your heart" two inclinations and here when evil inclination removed they had only one heart; and verse writes "in joy and good heart" and adjoins good to heart — more plausible for his midrash that it refers to song where evil inclination is not removed by song alone but by Torah which is its spice — then still two hearts unlike there where written "his heart was good" properly expounded on Torah study for when engaged in it it protects and prays; and they said three who ate at one table and spoke words of Torah etc. see what is written in introduction responsa Beit Ephraim OC section 1 and "they went to their tents joyful and good of heart" etc. — this is what we say "enlighten our eyes in Your Torah" — intent through Your Torah as Chazal said the light in it returns to good and then "our heart clings to Your commandments" etc. that two hearts unite to be one for love etc. which causes heart to cling to mitzvot after no nearby inclination; especially one should urge himself in Torah where there is some joy even mitzvah joy; see end Sukkah regarding joy of water-drawing and explained above siman 529 — a person eats drinks and rejoices on the festival and should not extend to flesh wine and laughter and lightheadedness since laughter and lightheadedness are not joy but frivolity and foolishness and we were not commanded on frivolity and foolishness but on joy that includes service of the Creator — so Rambam z"l and commentators explained on laughter I said of frivolity meaning in any matter where laughter is frivolity Avodat Yisrael above; but for joy what does it do — meaning regarding joy one cannot decide it is not fine since sometimes there is mitzvah joy therefore give heart to know what it does — what good if mitzvah joy or not; but since possible from eating drinking and frivolity it extends to laughter and lightheadedness — take spice to sweeten joy with Torah and "the Almighty is his strength and joy" and "his heart is good" in Torah; and he said "good heart continual feast" — may we have one heart to our Father in heaven and lift our hearts with hands to the Opener of hand in repentance may our words be acceptable before the Majestic One of all desires to attend doors of Torah and mitzvah to straighten path in ways of life; and whoever supplies them with garments or signs them departing with shields at gates of repentance — and the hand of Ephraim enlighten eyes and call the name of the place Machanaim: and may the Almighty restore our captivity in the gathering of Zion and Jerusalem and they shall be one — tree of Judah with tree of Joseph which (is in the hand of Ephraim):
